title: Cloud KMS Key Rotation Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.31 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.31 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="*CryptoKey*"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.31_cloud_kms_key_rotation_c_31"
| sort -_time
description: Crypto policy often mandates rotation; tracking next rotation time avoids audit findings and forced emergency rotations.
value: Detecting cloud kms key rotation compliance early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Nightly sync key metadata including rotation period and next rotation. Alert when rotation overdue or manual rotation gaps detected. Include CMEK keys for BigQuery and GCS.
visualization: Table (key, days to rotation), Timeline (rotation events), Single value (keys out of compliance).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Nightly sync key metadata including rotation period and next rotation. Alert when rotation overdue or manual rotation gaps detected. Include CMEK keys for BigQuery and GCS.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="*CryptoKey*"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.31_cloud_kms_key_rotation_c_31"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect cloud kms key rotation compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_31_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (key, days to rotation), Timeline (rotation events), Single value (keys out of compliance)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud kms key rotation compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
